A three-seed k=2-5 screening grid did not select k=3 unanimously: k=3 was selected in 2/3 MIMIC-IV, 1/3 eICU-CRD, and 2/3 AmsterdamUMCdb seeds, with k=2 selected otherwise; k=4-5 showed poor mixing. In the prespecified full-length K=2 versus K=3 experiment, all three K=3 initializations met the agreement, ARI, prevalence, and lag-1 criteria in MIMIC-IV and AmsterdamUMCdb, whereas only one of three did so in eICU-CRD. eICU-CRD therefore retained initialization sensitivity. The evidence supports recurrent broad trajectory shapes but does not establish k=3 as a unique biological taxonomy.

Before refitting, raw-event reconstruction established that the archived six-hour field represented the arithmetic mean of recorded events (99.993% exact agreement; mean absolute error 0.00064; one discrepancy among 14,846 evaluable windows). The documented-window sensitivity retained 1,043 patients and all three independent full-length initializations met the prespecified stability criteria (median agreement 0.835; median ARI 0.523; median NMI 0.438). The stricter ≥50%-coverage restriction retained 415 patients (29.3%); none of the three initializations met all criteria because the median PW fraction was zero and up to 41.7% of component-mean chains had high lag-1 autocorrelation. We therefore retain the broad trajectory-shape finding while explicitly stating that documentation density, selected-cohort restriction, and model convergence limit the stability of individual assignments.

The principal independent endpoint is 28-day mortality. We fitted cohort-specific binomial generalized linear models with HC3 robust standard errors, adjusting for age, sex, AKI stage at first diagnosis, log-transformed baseline SCr, and onset nonrenal SOFA score. Relative to RR, adjusted ORs for DR and PW were 2.89 (95% CI 2.41–3.46) and 9.89 (95% CI 7.73–12.66) in MIMIC-IV; 1.93 (95% CI 1.29–2.89) and 8.40 (95% CI 5.23–13.48) in eICU-CRD; and 2.03 (95% CI 1.59–2.59) and 5.56 (95% CI 4.03–7.67) in AmsterdamUMCdb.

In a restricted first-dose 24-hour landmark analysis among treated patients, response was not consistently associated with 28-day mortality: adjusted OR 0.592 (95% CI 0.331–1.060; P = 0.078) in MIMIC-IV and 1.129 (95% CI 0.567–2.249; P = 0.729) in AmsterdamUMCdb. The response-by-phenotype interaction was present in MIMIC-IV (P = 0.040) but not AmsterdamUMCdb (P = 0.785), and no phenotype-specific pattern replicated across cohorts. We retain these results only as exploratory associations in the Supplement and explicitly distinguish the analysis from a standardized furosemide stress test and from estimation of a treatment effect.

We also compared the exact-version replay of the archived AutoGluon XGBoost_BAG_L2 model with a simple six-variable multinomial logistic comparator using minimum and maximum SCr, minimum and maximum SCr/baseline SCr ratio, and minimum and mean urine output on the same evaluation splits. The archived model showed only small internal gains and no external incremental value: external macro OvO AUC was 0.769 for both models, while balanced accuracy (0.528 versus 0.578), macro F1 (0.504 versus 0.583), and Brier score (0.576 versus 0.407) favored the simpler model. Figure S12 now shows one-versus-rest quantile-bin calibration for the exact-version archived replay (upper row) and the six-variable comparator (lower row) in the internal and external cohorts; the fixed-parameter XGBoost sensitivity reanalysis is reported separately in Table S17c. We removed all claims of immediate bedside actionability. Prospective calibration, incremental-value, and decision-utility studies remain necessary.
